.. py:type:: LiberoSuiteName
   :canonical: Literal['libero_spatial', 'libero_object', 'libero_goal', 'libero_10', 'libero_90']


.. py:class:: LiberoEnvStepReturn

   Bases: :py:obj:`robo_orchard_core.envs.env_base.EnvStepReturn`\ [\ :py:obj:`LiberoObsType`\ , :py:obj:`LiberoRewardType`\ ]


   The return type of the `step` function in the environment.

   This class extends gymnasium's Env step return type to be a dataclass
   with generic types for observations and rewards.


   Template Args:
       ObsType: The type of the observations returned by the environment.
       RewardsType: The type of the rewards returned by the environment.



   .. py:attribute:: observations
      :type:  LiberoObsType

      The observations returned by the environment after taking a step.


   .. py:attribute:: terminated
      :type:  bool

      done flag


   .. py:attribute:: rewards
      :type:  LiberoRewardType

      The rewards is a [0,1] value indicating whether the task was successful.


   .. py:attribute:: truncated
      :type:  bool | None

      For evaluation environments, whether the episode was truncated due to
      reaching the step limit. Otherwise always None.


   .. py:attribute:: info
      :type:  dict[str, Any]

      Auxiliary information returned by the environment.


.. py:function:: get_libero_task(suite_name: str, task_id: int) -> LiberoTask

   Get the Libero task information.

   :param suite_name: The name of the Libero task suite.
   :type suite_name: str
   :param task_id: The ID of the task within the suite.
   :type task_id: int

   :returns: The Libero task information.
   :rtype: LiberoTask


.. py:class:: LiberoEnv(cfg: LiberoEnvCfg)

   Bases: :py:obj:`robo_orchard_core.envs.env_base.EnvBase`


   Base class for all environments.

   The environment is a class that comprise of all components and
   functions required to interact with.

   Specifically, the environment provides a `step` function, which
   takes in an action and returns the information about observations,
   rewards, and other information.


   This class is a simplified version of the gymnasium environment
   interface, which is used to define the environment for reinforcement
   learning tasks. We simplify the interface to provide a more generic
   and interface for environments.


   Template Args:
       EnvStepReturnType: The type of the return value of the `step` function.



   .. py:attribute:: cfg
      :type:  LiberoEnvCfg


   .. py:method:: step(action: ArrayLike) -> LiberoEnvStepReturn

      Take a step in the environment.

      Libero uses OSC (operational space control) actions, which are
      7-dimensional vectors representing the desired end-effector
      movements in the x, y, z directions and rotations around those axes,
      as well as the gripper open/close command (-1 = open, +1 = close).

      See :class:`robosuite.controllers.osc.OperationalSpaceController`
      and :class:`robosuite.manipulator.Manipulator` for more details.

      This is the default action type for LiberoEnv, but users can also
      choose to use the target end-effector pose as action by setting
      `use_action_type` to "osc_delta_pose" in the config.
      In that case, the action should be a 7-dimensional vector representing
      the target end-effector pose (x, y, z, q_w, q_x, q_y, q_z) in world
      frame, followed by gripper command.

      Note: Different from step function in libero env, we force update
      the observations after each step to ensure that the observations
      are always up-to-date with the simulation state, as we observe that
      the observation from step is delayed. The value is very close to
      the one before the fix, but this ensures consistency of LiberoEnv,
      because some method of LiberoEnv directly access the simulation state.




   .. py:method:: get_sim_state() -> numpy.ndarray

      Get the current simulator state as a flattened tensor.



   .. py:method:: reset(seed: int | None = None, init_state: Any | None = None) -> tuple[LiberoObsType, dict]

      Reset the environment.

      :param seed: Seed for the environment's random
                   number generator. Defaults to None.
      :type seed: int | None, optional
      :param init_state: Initial state to set after
                         reset. Defaults to None.
      :type init_state: Any | None, optional



   .. py:property:: num_envs
      :type: int


      The number of instances of the environment that are running.

      For example, if the environment is a single instance, then this
      should return 1. This is the case for most classical environments.

      In the case of reforcement learning, usually a vectorized environment
      is used to run multiple instances of the environment in parallel to
      speed up the training process. In this case, this function should
      return the number of instances of the environment that are running.

      The number of instances of the environment is used in other parts of
      the code to manage the environment.


   .. py:property:: task_info
      :type: robo_orchard_core.envs.task.TaskInfo


      Get the task information.


   .. py:method:: unwrapped_env() -> libero.libero.envs.OffScreenRenderEnv

      Get the original Libero environment.



   .. py:method:: get_robot_xml() -> str

      Get the robot XML used in the environment.

      Currently, Libero environments only support single-arm robots.

      :returns: robot XML strings.
      :rtype: str



   .. py:property:: eef_name
      :type: str


      Get the end-effector name of the robot.

      Currently, Libero environments only support single-arm robots.

      .. note::

         Libero uses the end-effector name defined in the robot controller,
         while the robot model may have a different end-effector name.
         This is a BUG in Libero, which we work around here by
         accessing the controller's end-effector name directly, as this
         is what Libero actually uses in the environment!

      :returns: The end-effector name of the robot.
      :rtype: str


   .. py:method:: get_arm_osc_delta_pose_from_target_pose(target_pose: robo_orchard_core.datatypes.BatchTransform3D, source_pose: robo_orchard_core.datatypes.BatchTransform3D) -> torch.Tensor

      Convert a target end-effector pose to an OSC delta action.

      This method requires that the input target_pose and source_pose
      have the same batch size, and the output OSC action will have
      the same batch size as well.



   .. py:method:: get_last_action() -> ActionInfo | None

      Get information about the last action taken in the environment.



   .. py:method:: close() -> None

      Close the environment.



   .. py:property:: control_timestep
      :type: float


      Get the average time interval between steps in the environment.

      In Libero, this value is around 1/20 seconds, corresponding to
      the control frequency of 20 Hz.

      :returns: The time interval between steps in seconds.
      :rtype: float


.. py:class:: LiberoEvalEnv(cfg: LiberoEvalEnvCfg)

   Bases: :py:obj:`LiberoEnv`


   Libero evaluation environment.

   The evaluation environment is used for benchmarking the performance
   of agents on the Libero tasks. The environment is configured to use a
   fixed set of initial states for each task, and the episode length is
   limited to a predefined number of steps based on the task suite.


   .. py:attribute:: cfg
      :type:  LiberoEvalEnvCfg


   .. py:attribute:: step_limits
      :type:  dict[str, int]

      Step limits for different Libero task suites.

      The value is copied from OpenVLA's Libero evaluation script.


   .. py:property:: step_limit
      :type: int



   .. py:method:: step(action: ArrayLike) -> LiberoEnvStepReturn

      Take a step in the environment.

      Libero uses OSC (operational space control) actions, which are
      7-dimensional vectors representing the desired end-effector
      movements in the x, y, z directions and rotations around those axes,
      as well as the gripper open/close command (-1 = open, +1 = close).

      See :class:`robosuite.controllers.osc.OperationalSpaceController`
      and :class:`robosuite.manipulator.Manipulator` for more details.

      This is the default action type for LiberoEnv, but users can also
      choose to use the target end-effector pose as action by setting
      `use_action_type` to "osc_delta_pose" in the config.
      In that case, the action should be a 7-dimensional vector representing
      the target end-effector pose (x, y, z, q_w, q_x, q_y, q_z) in world
      frame, followed by gripper command.

      Note: Different from step function in libero env, we force update
      the observations after each step to ensure that the observations
      are always up-to-date with the simulation state, as we observe that
      the observation from step is delayed. The value is very close to
      the one before the fix, but this ensures consistency of LiberoEnv,
      because some method of LiberoEnv directly access the simulation state.




   .. py:method:: reset(seed: int | None = None) -> tuple[LiberoObsType, dict]

      Reset the environment.

      :param seed: Seed for the environment's random
                   number generator. Defaults to None.
      :type seed: int | None, optional
      :param init_state: Initial state to set after
                         reset. Defaults to None.
      :type init_state: Any | None, optional



.. py:class:: LiberoEnvCfg

   Bases: :py:obj:`robo_orchard_core.envs.env_base.EnvBaseCfg`\ [\ :py:obj:`LiberoEnvType`\ ]


   Configuration for the RoboTwin environment.


   .. py:attribute:: class_type
      :type:  robo_orchard_core.utils.config.ClassType[LiberoEnvType]


   .. py:attribute:: suite_name
      :type:  LiberoSuiteName


   .. py:attribute:: task_id
      :type:  int


   .. py:attribute:: camera_heights
      :type:  int
      :value: 256



   .. py:attribute:: camera_widths
      :type:  int
      :value: 256



   .. py:attribute:: camera_depths
      :type:  bool
      :value: False



   .. py:attribute:: format_datatypes
      :type:  bool
      :value: False


      whether to format observation as robo_orchard datatypes.

      If True, the observation dict will be reformatted in the
      following way:
      - Camera data: replace with any rgb/depth camera keys containing
      BatchCameraData.
      - Robot joint data: replaced with 'joints' key containing
      BatchJointsState.
      - Robot frame transforms: replaced with 'tf_world' key containing
      BatchFrameTransform.


   .. py:attribute:: use_action_type
      :type:  typing_extensions.Literal[libero, orchard_osc_target_eef]
      :value: 'libero'


      The type of action to use in the environment:
      - "libero": use the original Libero action type defined in the robot
      controller.
      - "orchard_osc_target_eef": use the target end-effector pose as the action,
      which will be converted to OSC delta pose internally in the environment.


.. py:class:: LiberoEvalEnvCfg

   Bases: :py:obj:`LiberoEnvCfg`\ [\ :py:obj:`LiberoEvalEnv`\ ]


   Configuration for the RoboTwin evaluation environment.


   .. py:attribute:: class_type
      :type:  robo_orchard_core.utils.config.ClassType[LiberoEvalEnv]


   .. py:attribute:: episode_idx
      :type:  int

      Index of the evaluation episode.

      This is used to select the initial state from the predefined set
      of initial states for evaluation.


   .. py:attribute:: num_steps_wait
      :type:  int
      :value: 15


      Number of steps to wait after setting the initial state.
